clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old Syrian male with a history of alcoholism and heavy smoking presented with a 3-year history of persistent, unilateral hyperpigmented itchy patches on the right trunk and lateral right thigh. Clinical examination revealed hyperpigmented patches without telangiectasias, scaling, or atrophy. Skin biopsy histopathology demonstrated parakeratosic hyperkeratotic epidermis with slight spongiosis and moderate atypical lymphocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis with basilar distribution along the dermoepidermal junction, accompanied by mild melanophage deposition. Immunochemistry showed CD3+, CD8+, CD4−, CD20− atypical lymphocytes, consistent with a cytotoxic T-cell phenotype. Staging CT of chest and abdomen revealed no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. The patient was treated with PUVA therapy (oral 8-methoxypsoralen twice weekly) and topical 0.1% betamethasone dipropionate for 12 weeks, resulting in relief of itching and regression of hyperpigmentation, though incomplete clearance persisted.
